caption: California v. Trombetta
node: fair-trial-and-reliability-doctrines/Brady and Giglio (new sibling doctrine: duty to preserve evidence)
justification: Unanimous (Marshall, J.). Anchor of the due-process DUTY-TO-PRESERVE line, distinct from Brady's duty to disclose. The Due Process Clause does not require police to preserve breath samples in DUI cases; the constitutional duty to preserve evidence is limited to evidence that (1) possesses an exculpatory value APPARENT BEFORE it was destroyed, and (2) is of such a nature that the defendant cannot obtain comparable evidence by other reasonably available means. Directly governs officer/lab evidence-handling in the field. Corpus has NO duty-to-preserve doctrine at all (Brady/Giglio page is disclosure-only); grep 0 across content/cases, manifest, and all S6 queues. Strong page-candidate — the missing sibling of Brady on the fair-trial page.
gate: INGEST — suppression-side / officer field evidence-handling (mirror of the 'Brady cop' theory already paged)
notes: Not in GAP/sweep/gated/queue. Pairs with Youngblood + Fisher as the duty-to-preserve trilogy; Trombetta supplies the 'materially exculpatory (apparent value)' prong that Fisher later contrasts with 'potentially useful.'

caption: Arizona v. Youngblood
justification: 6-3 (Rehnquist, C.J.). The controlling rule for the more common case: for evidence that is only 'POTENTIALLY USEFUL' (as opposed to materially/apparently exculpatory under Trombetta), a defendant must show the police acted in BAD FAITH in failing to preserve it — negligence, poor judgment, or a good-faith mistake is not a due-process violation (failure to refrigerate/timely test biological evidence in a child-sexual-assault case). The single most-cited evidence-preservation holding; frames every police-lost-evidence / spoliation suppression motion. Corpus lacks it entirely (grep 0). Strong page-candidate; the anchor of the trilogy.
notes: Not in GAP/sweep/gated/queue. The 'bad faith' definition was left open to the lower courts (government-friendly divergence) and MANY state high courts reject the bad-faith requirement under their own constitutions — a state-departure frontier (see the mention row), analogous to the Manson->state-Henderson pattern the corpus already handles as mention-only.

caption: Illinois v. Fisher
justification: Per curiam. The modern reaffirmation/clarification: the Youngblood BAD-FAITH requirement applies to 'potentially useful' evidence REGARDLESS of a pending discovery request — the presence of a discovery request does NOT convert potentially-useful evidence into materially-exculpatory evidence or eliminate the bad-faith showing (destroyed suspected-cocaine substance, tested four times as positive, destroyed in the ordinary course while defendant was a fugitive). Completes the Trombetta->Youngblood->Fisher trilogy and closes the 'but I asked for it' argument. Corpus lacks it (grep 0). BORDERLINE page vs. fold-as-progeny-bullet under a Youngblood-anchored page — recommend page to keep the trilogy whole; S6 may fold to a Youngblood bullet under D5.
notes: Not in GAP/sweep/gated/queue. Distinguish Michigan v. Fisher (555 U.S. 45 (2009), emergency-aid) which IS in corpus — different case, do not merge.

caption: (mention) Youngblood 'bad faith' definition open + state-constitutional departures
justification: BELOW the D5 split-marker floor — recorded honestly, not a page-candidate. Two live frontiers on the Youngblood rule: (a) the Supreme Court left 'bad faith' undefined, and federal circuits diverge on what suffices (knowledge of exculpatory value, procedure-violation, motive) — a diffuse divergent-application, NOT a clean named both-sides circuit split; and (b) a substantial number of STATE high courts have REJECTED Youngblood's bad-faith requirement under their own constitutions, adopting a balancing/materiality test instead (state-departure pattern, mirrors the Manson->Henderson eyewitness departures the corpus treats as mention-only). No pending SCOTUS case. Floored to a mention; if a Youngblood-anchored page is authored, carry this as a Recent-developments state-departure note.
